text: The first 48 hours decide the file
This is the Waiz playbook for DSCR clients who work their own leads. No call center. No Laura. No setter pod. You — or your VA — are the system.
North star: show up like an operator, book the call while the lead is still hot, and never hang up without the next step on the calendar.

DSCR investors are not reverse-mortgage seniors. They already own rentals. They think in cash flow, equity, and deadlines. They reply faster. They also disappear faster. Ads create the conversation. You capture it. If you are late, another broker is not.
How to use this playbook
Read Chapter 01 so you stop treating these leads like seniors.
Believe the clock in Chapter 02. Speed is the offer.
Run the first 48 hours exactly as written. That is the file.
When they text back, call. Do not type a novel.
Never end a live conversation without a calendar hold (BAMFAM).
The drip is the safety net. It does not replace you.
What this covers — and what it does not

01  Why this ICP is different

These leads already own rentals. They are buying a better position on a property they already have — not a loan. Write-offs killing DTI. A balloon coming due. Idle equity sitting in a door. That changes follow-up.

text: Treat every new DSCR lead like a bid that expires. Not with fake scarcity. With speed.
They opted in because something is live right now. If you wait until Thursday to work leads, that file is already talking to someone else.
Same four pillars. Different human.
Availability, speed, personalization, and volume still apply. This playbook does not rewrite them. It applies them to an operator.

text: 02  The data — why speed wins

You do not need a speech. You need to believe the clock. This ICP is more responsive than a senior RM lead, so the data hits harder. They will pick up. They will text back. They will also take the next broker’s calendar link if you leave them on read.

text: 03  The first 48 hours
This is the file. Everything after Day 2 is recovery.

caption: Hour 0: call, double-dial, voicemail and text. Do all three. Do not pick one.

text: Hour 0 — they just opted in
Call. Now. From a number they can save.
If no answer: double-dial immediately. Many phones silence call one and let call two through.
Voicemail + text in the same breath. Who you are, DSCR refinance on a rental, one clear ask.
First SMS
[First name] — [Your name] here. Saw you came through on a DSCR refinance. I qualify these on the property’s rent, not your tax returns. Got 10 minutes today? (Txt STOP to opt out)
Voicemail
[First name], [Your name] — you asked about a DSCR refi on a rental. I can tell you in one short call whether the property even makes sense. I’ll text you this number. Call or text me back.
Rest of Day 1 and Day 2

04  How you respond
This chapter is the operating system. Memorize the table. Use the lines.

caption: A reply is a hand-raise. Calling is how you book. Do not write a paragraph.

text: They texted. Call them.
Do not write: thanks for getting back, I’d love to learn more, what does next week look like. Ring them. If they do not pick up:
Just called — easier to do this live. You around for 8 minutes?
If they insist on texting: one question, then the book.
Got it. Is this a rental you already own that you want to refinance? I can look at it on a short call today — 11:30 or 4:00. Which is less annoying?
First 15 seconds
Peer. Not closer-voice. Not a courtesy call from the team.
[First name], it’s [Your name] — you came through on the DSCR refinance. I don’t want to waste your time. Is now a terrible moment?
If yes → BAMFAM. If no:
Cool. Quick version: I look at rentals you already own. Qualification is the property’s rent versus the payment — not your W-2. What prompted you to look at this?
Then shut up. They will tell you write-off, balloon, or idle equity. That is the call.
Availability
Take calls when investors actually answer — early, lunch, late afternoon. Not only 10–2 Tuesday.
Offer two concrete times, 15-minute increments if you can. Whenever you’re free next week is how you lose.
Inbound, outbound, and a booking link. Walk them onto the calendar while you are on the phone.
Same-day is the goal. Next day is fine. Day-after is the ceiling. Past 72 hours is an objection, not a preference.
05  Contact rate and conversation rate
These are two different problems. Do not mix the medicine.

Call, text, email. Start on all three if you have them. Continue where they answered.
Short texts. Two or three lines. Not a block. Front-load Days 1–2. Do not diagnose the lead on touch one.

06  BAMFAM

BAMFAM = Book A Meeting From A Meeting. You never end a live conversation with I’ll send some times or I’ll follow up later. On DSCR this matters more, not less. This ICP will not sit in limbo. If you leave the next step in no-man’s-land, they take the next broker’s slot.

text: Word tracks — investor tone
They don’t have time right now
Totally fine — I’m not going to keep you. Let’s lock 12 minutes so we’re not playing tag. I’ve got tomorrow at 8:30 or 4:15. Which is less painful?
They want you to send times
I can text the link — I’ll do it right now while we’re on. Easier if we just pick: today at 5 or tomorrow at 9. I’ll hold it so it doesn’t disappear.
Pull forward
[Name], [Your name] — you’ve got us on Thursday. A slot opened this afternoon at 3:30. Want to knock the property out sooner so you’re not carrying it all week?
Confirm + save the contact
You’re set for Tuesday, 4:00 your time. I’ll call from this number. Save it as [Your name] — DSCR so it doesn’t look like spam. Texting the confirm now.
I’ll think about it
Fair. That’s why the first call is short — your numbers, whether the property even belongs in a DSCR box. Hold Wednesday at 11. Cancel if it’s not useful. Morning or afternoon better?
Do not argue. Do not pitch the loan. Book the look.
Anti-patterns

rows: Book next week now — then try to pull it forward
Text a calendar link and hang up
Stay on until the slot is on both calendars
Book 10 days out as the default
Let a VA circle back with times after the call
The live call is the booking window

text: 07  Show-rate hygiene
Booking is not the win. Show is the win. Investors no-show when the meeting feels optional or you went silent after the book.
Right after they book
Locked: [day], [time] [timezone] with me. I’ll call you. If the property details are handy (address + rent), grab them — we’ll go faster.
If they reply with a question — same hour. If the answer is longer than two sentences, call.
Reminders
Say the automated ones are automated. People do not mind reminders. They mind being lied to. Include the area code you will call from. Pickup roughly doubles when they recognize it.

rows: Confirm time, your name, number you will call from

text: If they go quiet after booking
Do not wait for the slot to no-show you. Call. One time, day before or morning of:
Still good for tomorrow at 4 — or do you want me to slide you to a time that actually works?
If they no-show: BAMFAM on the first connect. Do not send them back to the drip as if they were never booked.
08  The drip — safety net, not strategy
The drip covers the hours you are on other calls, in a closing, or asleep. It does not replace Chapters 03–06.
Day 1 of the drip is not a substitute for the 5-minute call. If you have no human speed-to-lead, Day 1 is the first text — send it the minute they land (quiet hours).
Any inbound reply → kill the drip. Then Chapter 04: call them.
Any book → kill the drip. Then Chapter 07.
STOP → kill immediately.
One sender identity. You. Not the team, not Laura, not a bot pretending to be you.
Paste file: 10-Day DSCR Self-Serve CRM Drip — LO first person. Copy SMS into your CRM. Exit on reply, book, and STOP.
